text:
The most powerful refutation of Bentham’s felicific calculus is that it is impossible to calculate all the consequences of one’s acts, so the calculus can never actually be carried out. Intensity, duration, certainty, propinquity, fecundity, purity, and extent therefore cannot be summed into a usable total. The method fails as a decision procedure before any comparison of pleasures is reached.

CONFIDENCE: 74
